newsitem.title: UK: GEC-Marconi unit axing 535 jobs over two yrs.
newsitem.headline: GEC-Marconi unit axing 535 jobs over two yrs.

text.p: GEC-Marconi Communications, a division of defence engineering giant General Electric Co Plc, is to axe 535 jobs at its UK plant in Chelmsford over the next two years due to falling orders, the group said on Wednesday.

Alan Tull, director of corporate relations at GEC-Marconi Communications, blamed the job cuts on "falling orders and also a greater software content" in products, which had led to more out-sourcing of components. "This has had an impact on our manufacturing jobs," he told Reuters.

The job losses would be "across the board -- ranging from the shop floor to management", said Tull. GEC-Marconi did not disclosed the cost of the redundancies which will be spread over a two-year period.

Commenting on the reasons behind the fall in orders, Tull told Reuters, "In general terms, defence business orders have been declining. In addition we've seen (industry) consolidation which has led to a smaller number of larger firms competing more agressively in the market place. We're all chasing a smaller market."
The division currently employs 3,900 people at its Chelmsford plant and makes products ranging from broadcast radio communications to field communications equipment for the defence industry.
